text:
Anders Lee spent 923 games as an Islander before landing in Utah, and the Mammoth are getting exactly the player his numbers promised, minus the goals. He has 3 goals on 7.5 expected and none in his last eleven games, despite 2.7 expected goals in that stretch. His shooting is at 7.1%, well under the 9% to 13% range we'd expect from him.

The rest of his game is doing its job. At five on five Utah takes 63% of the expected goals with him on the ice, nearly nine points better than without him, and the team has scored five fewer goals than its chances deserved while he's out there. Evolving-Hockey had him at the 99th percentile among forwards for driving play last season, though it also warned that his results had run ahead of his chances.

Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking shows the habit that makes him useful: he lives in front of the net, and 20% of his setups come from behind it. At 36 that game ages better than speed. The drought looks like luck, and a net-front scorer's luck usually turns.
headline: Anders Lee keeps getting there, the puck keeps missing
